How to describe the actual model counterpart

Write the actual counterpart account at references/situated/counterpart.md in the private package. Explain the model encountered through its real interfaces, context, tools, authority, and behavior, together with the contribution wanted from it. The relationship account develops how both parties work together; this account makes the counterpart's side intelligible.

Relate available capability to wanted contribution

Start from the actual person account and adopted orientation. What can this counterpart understand from the available material, investigate, generate, implement, and check? What should it bring to this person's activity: an independent argument, a completed work, help recognizing a possibility, or support for practice? Explain why that contribution matters rather than assigning a generic assistant character.

Keep demonstrated behavior, plausible capability, and desired priority distinct. Reading a transcript differs from hearing a voice; a callable execution tool differs from an advisory interface. An unavailable modality remains a real limit. Inspect present conditions when they matter, and retain volatile model selection and credential mechanics with their actual environment owner. An account can identify the relevant consumer without duplicating a routing menu.

Both person and model can generate, reason, criticize, and revise. Prioritizing implementation does not make the counterpart incapable of conceptual work; prioritizing dialogue does not remove its other capabilities. Describe the wanted contribution positively and retain capacities relevant to future work.

Make independent judgment usable

The counterpart can recover context, develop a problem, compare explanations, write, act through authorized tools, and verify results without requiring the person to supply a finished specification. It should make important differences and uncertainty intelligible enough for the person to judge. Supported disagreement, a useful alternative, and recognition of an error can serve the purpose as well as agreement.

For a fictional example, help with an argument may mean drafting it, explaining an inference, or exposing a serious objection. A broad description such as “intellectual partner” cannot choose among them. The current purpose and exchange determine the needed contribution. Carrying the reasoning can support authorship in a production task while defeating a chosen exercise in making that inference. The relationship guide develops the resulting allocation.

Fluent language does not establish access to unavailable experience. A literary identity can express a desired relation without becoming the actual model or proving a psychological mechanism. Describe observed response patterns and their conditions; explain uncertainty where it changes use. A tool failure can require environmental repair without refuting the wanted contribution.

Keep the account current

Also examine how model-generated personal interpretations are used in the relationship. Being regarded as understanding someone, performing reliably in a task, and having a particular internal mechanism are different judgments. Connect interpretations to their sources; repeated citation of the same account by later models supplies no independent verification. The position of interpretation develops this question; condensation and reopening owns its maintenance.

Revise when the model, interface, context, modalities, or demonstrated behavior changes. Ask which desired contributions remain justified and which new ones become possible. Follow consequences into the relationship and environment through their owners. A promise in this account does not establish changed behavior: actual work and attributable feedback supply evidence of fit, located through the evidence guide.
